bc_quagmire_area.blurb: Quagmire Area is a trad crag on the central face of the Malamute, the cliff above Squamish. It has five lines, nearly all of them cracks in granodiorite. Four sit in the 5.10 range, from 5.10a to 5.10d, and one is a much harder 5.12 test piece, so it suits climbers already leading steady mid-grade cracks on a standard rack. The Malamute as a whole is often windy and stays in shade until about one in the afternoon, which can feel chilly outside summer.

bc_overly_hanging_out_2.blurb: Overly Hanging Out is a small crag at the far southern end of the Malamute near Squamish. It has five lines in granodiorite, three trad and two sport, and one of the trad lines runs three pitches. The range is lopsided: one easy 5.6 and one 5.10, with the other three at 5.11. That puts it mainly in front of strong leaders who want steeper, harder climbing with a short list of choices. Like the rest of the Malamute, it tends to be breezy and holds shade until about one in the afternoon.

bc_zebra_wall.blurb: Zebra Wall is a roadside sport wall along Arrow Lake outside Castlegar, in the West Kootenay. It has five bolted lines, ranging from an easy 5.9 through three 5.10 routes to a single 5.11, so most of the grade spread suits a climber working through the lower double digits. The wall is vertical and built from dark dyke rock; staying on the line of the route matters because loose pieces can come off. Being a short walk from the car makes it a quick stop for a session rather than a full day out.
bc_zebra_wall.parking_note: Drive Broadwater Road past the pulp mill, the dam and the marina; the wall is a short way beyond the marina, and you leave the car at a roadside pullout there.
bc_zebra_wall.approach: A short walk of a couple of minutes along the road from the pullout leads directly to the wall.

bc_tombstone_tower.blurb: Tombstone Tower is a small crag within Cypress Falls Park near Vancouver. It has five routes, four of them trad and one sport, between 5.8 and 5.11 in difficulty: an easy line at 5.8, one at 5.10, and three at 5.11. Climbs are short, around 10 to 15 metres, and the terrain is a mix of steep and vertical faces among conifers. A small rack of cams up to about 3 inches covers the gear lines, and bolts protect the cruxes of several harder ones. Expect to share the park with hikers on the way in.
bc_tombstone_tower.approach: From the park's main trail, turn off just before a black fence and follow a path toward the river. The walk takes roughly 7 minutes, and a fixed handline helps on the steep final bank down to the base.

bc_midway_wall.blurb: Midway Wall is a small sport wall within Nordic Rock, in the Sea to Sky corridor between Squamish and Whistler. It sits just left of and below the Main Wall, so it can be combined with that wall in one outing. Five bolted routes make up the wall: three in the 5.10 range, from 5.10a to 5.10c, and two harder ones at 5.11. The rock is andesite.

bc_beach_boys.blurb: Beach Boys is a sector of The Beach, a sport crag beside the Trans-Canada Highway west of Kamloops. It has five bolted lines and a wider spread than most small walls: a very easy line, a 5.7, two 5.10 routes and one 5.11, so a beginner and a stronger partner can both find something. It is the newest wall at The Beach, still being developed, and some routes can be a bit dirty. Routes at the crag are bolted with chain anchors and run roughly 7 to 20 metres.

bc_century_wall.blurb: Century Wall is one of the sport sectors at Horne Lake on Vancouver Island. It has five bolted routes at a notably high level: one at 5.10, two at 5.11, one at 5.12 and one at 5.13. It is aimed at strong climbers rather than those new to leading outdoors. The rock is limestone, and the wall is reached by a trail with a few switchbacks up from the parking lot.
